madhurā.notes: MN 84 places Mahākaccāna in Madhurā and names its king Avantiputta. The journey between Madhurā and Verañjā is in AN 4.53. The page placements also include the unrelated MN 83 and AN 4.52.

magadha.notes: The comparison with Magadhan village fields is in AN 5.100. AN 5.99 is a lion simile. The packet misses Magadha in the sixteen-country lists in AN 3.70, AN 8.42, AN 8.43 and AN 8.45, where the English names the countries one segment before the Pali. Snp 5.19:28.1 also names the country in its closing verses.

magha.notes: SN 11.12:1.3 and SN 11.13:6.1 explicitly give Magha as Sakka’s former human name. SN 11.11 gives his seven vows. The placements at SN 11.9, SN 11.10 and SN 11.14 do not supply either passage.

mahisavatthu.notes: AN 8.8:1.1 confirms Uttara and Saṅkheyyaka. Sujato takes Mahisavatthu as the region containing the mountain, while the entry describes it as a place on the mountain.

mahākaccāna.notes: AN 1.197 names the foremost interpreter of a brief statement, and MN 18 gives his explanation. The alternative form Mahākaccāyana occurs at MN 118:1.3 and in the attribution at Thag 8.1:8.7. Check the entry’s AN.i.84f reference to an Apadāna story and its AN.iii.192 reference for Tapodā. Neither AN 5.165 nor AN 5.166 names the elder. Other page placements include neighboring texts such as AN 6.25, AN 10.25, MN 83, SN 22.2 and SN 35.131.

mahāli.notes: Mahāli the Licchavi asks about Sakka in SN 11.13 and about Pūraṇa Kassapa’s claim in SN 22.60. The citations also land on the preceding SN 11.12 and SN 22.59. AN 10.50 names Mahāli only in its chapter recap.

mahānāma.notes: Each Sakyan assignment explicitly calls Mahānāma a Sakyan, including AN 1.252 on fine gifts. AN 5.58:3.1 calls the man in the Great Wood a Licchavi. AN 5.57 is a neighboring page hit. The Sakyan’s lodging search and question on concentration are in AN 3.126 and AN 3.73 respectively. SN 11.3 concerns Sakka’s banner. MN 116:6.25 names the independent Buddha, and Thag 1.115 attributes the verse to the elder, repeated in the recap at Thag 1.120. Neither has a candidate entry. AN 8.30, AN 11.21, SN 55.30 and SN 55.40 mention Mahānāma only in chapter recaps. Snp 5.19:25.4 describes the third chapter of the anthology.

mahāpāragā.notes: DN 20:16.7–8 names the Pāragā and Mahāpāragā among the assembled gods. The entry identifies the discourse by title, but its DN.ii.26 citation lands in DN 14.

mahāsammata.notes: The reference list has no placement. DN 27:20.3–21.1 tells of the people electing one person, giving a share of their rice and applying the designation Mahāsammata. Sujato translates the title as ‘popularly elected’.

mahāvana.notes: AN 9.41:1.1–1.6 places this Great Wood at Uruvelakappa among the Mallas, and AN 9.41:5.2 has Ānanda take Tapussa to the Buddha there. The citation lands in AN 9.40. The packet reports zero mentions, though Sujato’s ‘Great Wood’ also renders mahāvana at Vesālī in MN 36:1.2 and at Kapilavatthu in MN 18:2.2. Those two forests need their own entries.

mahī.notes: The packet misses the river in SN 13.3, SN 13.4, SN 55.42, SN 56.53 and SN 56.54. In each, the English names Mahī one segment before the Pali list. SN 13.5 uses a simile about earth instead.

makkhaligosāla.notes: Snp 3.6:2.2 spells the teacher’s name as one word. DN 2:3.2 and SN 2.30:3.1 use two words, which accounts for their absence from this lemma’s mentions. The exchange with Saccaka naming him is in MN 36, although the citation lands in MN 35. AN 3.137 and AN 6.57 name him, while AN 3.135–136 and AN 6.56 are neighboring placements. SN 22.60 is a comparison of doctrines and attributes the teaching there to Pūraṇa Kassapa.

mallikā.notes: AN 5.49 reports Queen Mallikā’s death to Pasenadi. The adjacent AN 5.50 concerns Queen Bhaddā and King Muṇḍa. Mallikā’s park is in MN 78, the conversation on self-love in SN 3.8, and the birth of her daughter in SN 3.16. The page placements also include MN 77, SN 3.9 and SN 3.17. AN 8.91–117 gives the laywoman’s name alone. AN 8.118–119 begin a new series. AN 4.200, SN 3.10 and SN 3.20 also mention Mallikā in chapter recaps.

mandākinī.notes: AN 7.66:6.2–3 lists Mandākinī among the lakes from which the rivers flow. The entry covers the lake part of the DPD gloss.

manopadosikā.notes: The packet reports zero mentions. DN 1:2.10.2 and DN 24:2.19.9 explicitly name these gods and describe how their mutual anger leads to their passing away. DN 20:16.4 lists them at the assembly. Sujato translates the name as ‘malevolent’.

mantāṇī.notes: MN 86:12.11–12 gives Aṅgulimāla’s answer about his parents’ clans, including ‘mantāṇī mātā’. DPD’s MN 24 example names Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, a different son, and provides no evidence for this identification.

maṅgala.notes: MN 116:3.7–9 introduces the roll of independent Buddhas that names Maṅgala at 6.29.

maṇibhadda.notes: SN 10.4 gives the encounter at the Maṇimālika shrine. The page also picks up SN 10.3 on Sūciloma and SN 10.5 on Sānu. The mention in SN 10.12:14.2 is a chapter recap.
